en: to be loving; to be caring

examples.en: My grandmother always speaks in a warm, kind voice.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 다정스럽게 손을 잡고 걸어요.
examples.en: The two of them walk hand in hand affectionately.

examples.ko: 새로 온 선생님이 다정스러워서 학생들이 좋아해요.
examples.en: The new teacher is warm, so the students like her.

examples.ko: 옆집 아저씨는 다정스럽지는 않지만 마음이 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The man next door is not affectionate, but he has a warm heart.
The way he held the child looked so tender.

examples.ko: 다정스러운 말 한마디에 하루가 달라질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes one kind word can change your whole day.

explain: '다정하다'와 뜻이 거의 같고, '-스럽다'가 붙어 그런 분위기나 태도가 느껴진다는 뜻이 더해져요. 사람의 말투, 표정, 모습을 꾸며 줄 때 어울려요. ㅂ불규칙이라 '다정스러워요', '다정스러운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Mom called me in a loving voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요. 말투나 목소리가 따뜻하게 느껴질 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, fitting when a tone or voice feels warm.

phrases.en: The teacher spoke to the students affectionately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸며 주는 부사형이에요. 행동이나 말하는 방식을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form that modifies a verb, used to describe how someone acts or speaks.

phrases.en: The two of them are really affectionate.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite 해요 form of '다정스럽다', changing to '다정스러워요' because it is ㅂ-irregular.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '다정하다', and the '-스럽다' ending adds the sense that the warmth can be felt in someone's manner. It fits a person's voice, expression, or look. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '다정스러워요' and '다정스러운'.

en: in affectionate whispers; with affectionate murmuring

examples.en: The family gathers and chats in warm, quiet voices.
I can hear soft, friendly voices from the kitchen.

examples.ko: 친구와 도란도란 얘기하다 보니 시간이 훌쩍 갔어요.
examples.en: Chatting cozily with my friend, the time flew by.
I listened to old stories next to my grandmother in a cozy, quiet way.

examples.ko: 아이들이 이불 속에서 도란도란 속삭이고 있어요.
examples.en: The children are whispering cozily under the blanket.
Shall we talk quietly as we walk?

explain: '소곤소곤'은 작은 목소리에 초점이 있지만, '도란도란'은 정답고 화목한 분위기까지 담겨 있어요. 보통 '이야기하다, 말하다, 속삭이다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 싸우거나 긴장된 대화에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.example: 저녁에 가족과 도란도란 이야기하며 밥을 먹어요.
phrases.en: In the evening I eat while chatting warmly with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정답게 이야기하는 모습에 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for chatting warmly.

phrases.en: The children whisper cozily in bed.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a feeling of speaking softly and affectionately.

phrases.en: In the library, we speak in whispers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 목소리에 초점이 있고, 정다운 분위기는 꼭 없어도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on a small voice and doesn't need a warm mood.

explain_en: '소곤소곤' focuses on a small voice, but '도란도란' also carries a warm, friendly mood. It usually goes with verbs like '이야기하다', '말하다' and '속삭이다'. It doesn't suit an argument or a tense conversation.

en: to put arms around each other's shoulders

examples.en: We walked home with our arms around each other's shoulders.

examples.ko: 아이들이 어깨동무해서 한 줄로 서 있어요.
examples.en: The kids stand in a line with their arms over each other's shoulders.

examples.ko: 친한 친구끼리 어깨동무하면 사진이 더 정다워 보여요.
examples.en: When close friends put their arms around each other, the photo looks warmer.
We sang the cheer song with our arms around each other.
After we put our arms around each other, we felt closer.
It's embarrassing to put an arm around someone you've just met.

explain: '어깨동무를 하다'를 한 단어처럼 쓴 말이에요. 서로 어깨에 팔을 두르는 것이라서, 팔을 끼는 '팔짱을 끼다'와 구분해서 써요.

phrases.en: My friend and I put our arms around each other's shoulders when taking the photo.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past tense, used to talk about something that already happened.
phrases.en_equiv: put arms around each other's shoulders (past)

phrases.en: Let's put our arms around each other!
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구에게 하는 반말 권유 표현이에요. 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual suggestion to close friends. Don't use it with someone older or senior.
phrases.en_equiv: let's put our arms around each other

phrases.en: The kids sing with their arms around each other's shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'로 이어서 다른 동작을 함께 하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -고 ending connects it to another action done at the same time.
phrases.en_equiv: to sing with arms around each other's shoulders

explain_en: It is '어깨동무를 하다' used as a single verb. It means two people put arms around each other's shoulders, which is different from '팔짱을 끼다', linking arms.

examples.en: A goddess of love appears in Greek mythology.

examples.ko: 이 동상은 바다의 여신을 만든 거예요.
examples.en: This statue depicts the goddess of the sea.

examples.ko: 여신 같은 분위기의 배우가 무대에 나왔어요.
examples.en: An actress with a goddess-like aura came onto the stage.
Fans call that singer a goddess.
People prayed to the goddess of a good harvest.
The children enjoy reading stories about goddesses.

explain: 남신은 남자 신이고 '여신'은 여자 신이에요. 신화에서 쓰지만 요즘은 아주 아름답거나 인기가 많은 여성을 칭찬하는 말로도 많이 써요. 이때는 '여신 미모'처럼 가볍게 말해요.

phrases.en: That actress looks like a goddess.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 아름다운 여성을 칭찬하는 가벼운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual compliment for a very beautiful woman.

phrases.en: A large statue of a goddess stands by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상'을 붙이면 여신을 본떠 만든 조각이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '상' means a statue made in the image of a goddess.

phrases.en: Today the goddess of victory was on our side.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~의 여신'은 신화 속 여신뿐 아니라 운이 좋았다는 표현에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Goddess of ~' is used for mythical goddesses and also for saying luck was on your side.

explain_en: A male deity is 남신 and a female deity is 여신. It is used in myths, but these days it is also a common compliment for a very beautiful or popular woman, as in '여신 미모'.

en: to be righteous; to be morally just

examples.en: He is a just police officer.
I want to build a just society.
The way they helped their friend is righteous.
Acting justly is not easy.
I think a person looks coolest when they are righteous.
He is just, so many people trust and follow him.

explain: '정의'에 '-롭다'가 붙은 말로 ㅂ 불규칙이라 '정의로워요', '정의로운'으로 바뀌어요. 사람이나 행동, 사회를 칭찬할 때 써요. 일상 대화보다 글이나 영화 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I want to be a righteous person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 앞에서 꾸며 주는 가장 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form used before a noun to describe a person.

phrases.en: The main character of that movie is really righteous.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes 정의로워요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 옳지 않다고 비판할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form used to criticize something as unfair.

explain_en: Built from the noun for justice plus a suffix, it is a b-irregular adjective, so it becomes the forms ending in 'wo'. It praises people, actions and societies, and shows up more in writing and movie talk than in daily chat.

dis.h: morally right, standing up for justice

p.n: '정의롭다' is morally righteous and brave about right and wrong; '공정하다' is fair-minded and unbiased.
